I'll plan my year the way I always do — start from what I did last year, adjust a little.

My land is 13.1 mu. Most of it I do wheat then maize, that's how everyone around here farms. I'll put about 10 mu on wheat-maize. Cotton I still keep 2 mu — old habit, and my wife spins some at home. Mungbean I plant 1.1 mu on the corner plot that doesn't get good water, mungbean doesn't need much.

For wheat I buy 2 bags of compound fertilizer (50 kg each of 15-15-15) per mu before ploughing, then topdress with about half a bag of urea at greening up. That's what my neighbor Old Wang does and he gets good wheat. I water it 4 times — after sowing, at greening, at jointing, at filling. Seed I buy the improved kind from the town dealer, "Jimai 22" type, everyone uses it.

For maize after wheat I just rotary till and plant directly, no time to plough. I use 1 bag compound at sowing and one bag of urea at big-trumpet stage. Water twice if no rain. I use hybrid seed, the dealer picks for me.

Cotton costs more work. I put 2 bags compound and topdress urea twice. Spray many times for bollworm — maybe 6 times. Water 3 times.

Mungbean I don't fertilize much, it makes its own. Just a handful of compound at planting. No irrigation, one spray if aphids come.

Every yuan counts with 7 mouths at home, so I don't waste fertilizer — but I'd rather put a little extra than lose grain. Losing grain is losing food.
